qs.q: A 24-year-old woman presents with a frothy, yellow-green vaginal discharge and a 'strawberry cervix' on speculum examination. Which of the following is the most likely causative organism?
qs.e: Trichomonas vaginalis is a flagellated protozoan that causes a frothy yellow-green discharge and characteristic strawberry cervix. Gardnerella vaginalis typically presents with a thin, grey-white fishy-smelling discharge and clue cells.
qs.s: Disorders of the Vagina and Breast: MCQs

qs.q: A clinician performs a Pap smear to screen a patient for malignancy of the cervix. Which branch of cytology does this minimally invasive procedure, utilizing cells obtained from body surfaces and mucous membranes, fall under?
qs.e: Exfoliative cytology involves studying cells obtained from body surfaces and membranes (such as skin or the cervix via Pap smear, urine, or bronchial washing) without the need to invade body organs. Aspiration cytology, by contrast, invades body organs to collect internal cells.

qs.q: Which of the following treatment approaches involves placing a radioactive source directly inside or near the tumor, such as in the cervix?
qs.e: Brachytherapy specifically involves placing a radioactive source inside or near the tumor. External beam radiation involves aiming radiation from outside the body.
qs.s: Oncology: Surgery, Radiotherapy & Chemotherapy Explained: MCQs

qs.q: A young female patient presents with a purulent vaginal discharge and is found to have prominent lymphoid follicles on histological examination of the cervix. Which organism is the most common cause of this condition, accounting for up to 40% of STD clinic presentations?
qs.e: Chlamydia trachomatis is the most common infectious cause of cervicitis and characteristically accounts for up to 40% of STD clinic cases while displaying prominent lymphoid follicles. Other pathogens include Ureaplasma and Trichomonas, but C. trachomatis is the leading agent.
qs.s: Female Reproductive Pathology: HPV, Cancer, PCOS & Pregnancy: MCQs

qs.q: In the pathological assessment of cervical neoplasia, where do these neoplastic changes predominantly originate within the cervix?
qs.e: Cervical neoplasia is predominantly an HPV-driven process that arises specifically within the transformation zone of the cervix. Persistent infection leads to CIN grades managed by severity using Pap smear screening.
qs.s: Female Reproductive Pathology: HPV, Cancer, PCOS & Pregnancy: MCQs

qs.q: A cervical tumour encircles the cervix and penetrates the underlying stroma deeply. This morphologic appearance is called
o: Described as a barrel cervix lesion
qs.e: When tumour encircles the cervix and invades the stroma, it produces a barrel cervix identifiable on direct palpation.

qs.q: A 55-year-old woman presents with vaginal bleeding. Imaging shows a tumour arising from the cervix and invading surrounding tissue. Which histologic type is most common? The majority of cervical cancers are squamous cell. ---
o: Adenocarcinoma, glandular malignant tumor of the cervix
Squamous cell carcinoma, the predominant cervical cancer type
Sarcoma, malignant tumor of mesenchymal origin in the cervix
Small cell carcinoma, neuroendocrine malignant tumor of the cervix
Clear cell carcinoma, rare malignant tumor with clear cytoplasm
qs.e: Squamous cell carcinoma accounts for the majority of cervical cancers.
qs.s: Pathology by Dr. Irungu — MCQ Bank
